Lick Creek Park In The Dark - LCN-41

Create fun memories with friends and family without traveling far away. Choose your adventure or join us for favorites, such as a hot dog dinner, nature presentations, s'mores and a night hike. Learn camping basics and discover the nocturnal creatures that call Lick Creek Park home.

The family-friendly overnight event begins at 6 p.m. Friday and ends at 7 a.m. Saturday. Campers must bring a tent, supplies, snacks, and drinks. Electricity is not provided, so pack flashlights, tent lanterns, sleeping bags, insect repellent, and folding chairs. Children must be accompanied by an adult (18+), and pets are not allowed. A limited number of spots are available, and registration ends the Wednesday before camp.

Schedule of Events
6 p.m. • Check-in and campsite set-up
6 p.m. • Special nature presentations, activities, s'mores, and games begin
7 p.m. • Hot dog dinner
7:30 p.m. • Night hikes begin
9 p.m. • Special nature presentations and night hikes end
9:45 p.m. • S'mores, activities, and games end
10 p.m. • Quiet hours begin

Registration • Aug. 3-Wednesday before camp

Walk Like an Engineer – Grandparents Day - LCN-96

Celebrate Grandparents Day with a hands-on class where grandparents and grandchildren explore how engineers design solutions inspired by nature. Walk with bio-inspired engineering experts from Texas A&M and nature educators as you learn about engineering design through thinking activities and hands-on exploration. The class takes place on paved surfaces and is ADA accessible for guests with mobility needs. Dress for the outdoors, wear closed-toed shoes and bring water.

Registration • Aug. 3-Sept. 12 at 5 p.m.

Jingle Bell Fun Run - PKS-01

For 36 years, the Jingle Bell Fun Run has been a fun, lighthearted way to kick off the holiday season in College Station. This year, College Station Parks and Recreation is putting a merry twist on the event with a new 1.5-mile route.

The untimed run takes place Saturday, Dec. 5, and runs along the parade route ahead of the College Station Christmas Parade, which begins at 4 p.m. Line-up starts at 3 p.m. at 810 Holleman Drive East, and the run begins at 3:30 p.m. The course ends at the entrance to Christmas in the Park at 1000 Krenek Tap Road, where the evening’s festivities continue from 6 to 10 p.m.

The early entry fee is $15 and includes a shirt and jingle bells if you register by Nov. 17. The cost is $20 during the Nov. 18-30 late registration period. Jingle bells are included, but you aren’t guaranteed a shirt. Participants 3 and under are free. Dogs are not allowed. Packet pickup is 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Dec. 2-3 and 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Dec. 4 at the Stephen C. Central Park office.

Race day parking is available at Post Oak Mall (old Macy’s side), where shuttles will run from 3 p.m. to midnight between the mall and Central Park.

Registration: Aug. 3-Nov. 29

Exploring History Luncheon - PKS-17

Enjoy lunch while learning about our community’s history. Lectures are presented in partnership with the College Station Historic Preservation Committee. Attendance is free, and lunch is $10 for residents or $12 for non-residents. A limited number of meals will be available at the door for $12.

Schedule Aug. 19 • “Aggieland Through Time: Mapping the Campus Past” by Ian Muise and Audrey Lloyd, historian and sesquicentennial archival research specialist at Cushing Memorial Library and Archives.

Sept. 16 • “And Then There Were Maggie's” by Linda Harvell, Chairperson of the Historic Preservation Committee and former City Councilwoman

Oct. 21 • “Millican Massacre of 1868” by Amy Earhart, associate professor of English and Africana studies faculty.

Nov. 18 • “College Station: A City Founded with Parks” by Steve Beachy, former College Station Parks and Recreation director, and Dr. John Crompton, Texas A&M professor in the Department of Recreation, Park and Tourism Sciences.

Dec. 9 • “Sweet Strings on the Brazos” by Nicki George, musician with Sweet Strings on the Brazos.

Registration ends the Friday before each luncheon.

Movie in the Park: Jurassic Park (PG-13) - PKS-31

Bring blankets, chairs and picnic baskets and enjoy an interactive outdoor movie night featuring Jurassic Park (PG-13) on a 32-foot inflatable screen. The evening includes a costume contest, trivia, food trucks and additional on-site activities. Free popcorn will be available while supplies last.

Dress as favorite characters or dinosaurs from the franchise and be ready for movie-themed trivia. Pre-registration is required. Prizes will be awarded for trivia winners and costume contest categories, including ages 0-12, ages 13 and up and family/group.

Parking is available at Post Oak Mall, with accessible parking near Colgate Drive. Pets are not allowed. Coolers must be 48 quarts or smaller. Glass containers and kegs are not allowed.

Schedule of Events
5 p.m. • Gates open and activities begin
6 p.m. • Costume contest
7 p.m. • Trivia
7:30 p.m. • Movie begins

Registration • Aug. 3-Nov. 5
